```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 15_related_anova_third_condition
title: Why not just subtract?
questions:
  - id: no_single_difference
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      In Chapter 13 we dealt with the differences between children by
      subtracting: each child's two times became one difference score, and we
      tested those. What's the problem with doing that here?
    options:
      - text: No single pairwise difference covers all three conditions
        correct: true
      - text: Subtracting would take out the differences between conditions too
      - text: With the same children in every condition, there are no differences between children to remove
    explanation: >
      With three conditions there are three pairs, so each child has three
      differences. We could test each one, but that brings back Chapter 14's
      problem of making several comparisons. Subtracting wasn't the issue:
      it keeps the differences between conditions, which is why it worked in
      Chapter 13. And the differences between children haven't gone anywhere.
      Using the same children keeps them out of the comparison between
      conditions, but some children are still faster than others in every
      condition. So we need another way of setting those differences aside.
```
